text:
maya-sales: Heads up — Helix Financial wants a short POC. Requirements: streaming with SSE fallback (corp proxies), structured function/tool-calls + schema versioning, TypeScript edge adapter, .NET backend orchestration, on-prem connector (VPC), SAML SSO, and offline KMS/HSM. Also asked for a quick pricing ballpark for 200 qps steady, spikes to 1k. Can eng/presales assemble blockers + a one-pager? :wave:

owen-eng: Got it. Quick q: will the TypeScript adapter open outbound connections only? That affects ephemeral token design.

maya-sales: Yes outbound-only from customer-managed host. They want tokens that rotate; security team prefers short TTLs (~5m).

lucy-ml: Streaming rec: prefer WebSocket for low-latency, SSE fallback for strict proxies. We can stream incremental tool_call.parts so UI shows partial args/results. Example SSE line we emit:

```json
{"evt":"tool_call.part","id":"t-901","payload":{"name":"fetch_account","partial":"{\"acct_id\":\"...\"}"}}
```

owen-eng: TS ephemeral token example (fetch):
```ts
const res = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${ephemeralToken}`,
    'X-Req-Id': reqId
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
})
```

kevin-se: On security: we provide SOC2, ISO summary, SAML SSO integration guide, and an HSM/KMS connector for Private deployments. For offline KMS tests we can supply test keys + connector docs. I'll share contacts and docs.

infra-bot: Note: Dedicated recommended if sustained >450 qps. Hosted can handle bursts but unit cost is higher. See /pricing/reserved-capacity for estimator.

maya-sales: Pricing — they want a quick ballpark to decide Dedicated vs hosted. Any rough numbers I can put in an email?

owen-eng: High-level: hosted pay-as-you-go tends to be ~2-3x per-token vs Dedicated. For 200 qps steady with spikes to 1k, recommend small Dedicated commit (1-3 GPUs depending on model) + hosted burst. Exact depends on model family and quantization; I'll follow up with a tighter range once they pick model.

lucy-ml: Structured output guidance: include schema_version and a structured.tool_calls array so our evals can validate and we can detect regressions. Preferred shape example:

```json
{
  "schema_version":"1.0",
  "response":"...",
  "structured":{
    "tool_calls":[{"name":"fetch_account","status":"complete","result":{"balance":123.45}}],
    "assertions":[{"id":"bal-nonneg","ok":true}]
  }
}
```

kevin-se: POC blockers checklist: 1) IP allowlist or site-to-site VPN/VPC peering, 2) exchange SAML metadata + test IdP, 3) temporary KMS/HSM test creds or connector access, 4) acceptance prompt set + perf targets, 5) confirm model family for cost estimate. If allowlist isn't feasible, we can run a short-lived outbound agent behind their edge host.

own-eng: .NET auth snippet for backend calls (HttpClient):
```csharp
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url);
req.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", ephemeralToken);
req.Headers.Add("X-Req-Id", reqId);
var resp = await httpClient.SendAsync(req);
```

maya-sales: Perfect. Can folks drop links/docs: allowlist IP ranges, SAML steps, ephemeral token examples (TS + .NET), dedicated estimator, and security contact/pack? I'll turn into a one-pager for the customer and request SAML metadata + network contact. Target POC kickoff in ~2 weeks if SAML & network cleared. :calendar: :thumbsup:

kevin-se: I'll DM SOC2 + pen-test summary and the security lead.

lucy-ml: I'll assemble structured-output examples + a tiny eval set that fails fast on malformed tool-calls.

own-eng: I'll prepare allowlist ranges, TS + .NET snippets, and a minimal runbook for the TypeScript edge adapter with WS/SSE fallback. Share by EOD tomorrow.

infra-bot: Reminder: request Dedicated trial form early if committing — GPU lead time ~3-4 weeks.

maya-sales: Thanks team. I'll draft the one-pager and loop in the customer's infra lead.

[thread end]
